newsitem.title: USA: Coastal Texas cat cracker shut last Friday.
newsitem.headline: Coastal Texas cat cracker shut last Friday.

text.p: Coastal Corp shut its 20,000 barrel per day catalytic cracking unit in Corpus Christi, Texas last Friday for unspecified unscheduled maintenance, Coastal spokesman Brian Mitchell said.
"We'll cover our deliveries by purchasing what we need in the market," Mitchell said, noting he did not know when the unit, part of Coastal's 95,000 bpd refinery, might be restored.

Some gasoline traders on the U.S. Gulf Coast (USG) said the outage gave cash gasoline values a slight lift, but others doubted the news could change a dim picture for refiners in the region, some of whom are losing money making gasoline.
"It doesn't pay to make gasoline in the Gulf. Eventually, refiners are facing the economics hurdle and we will see run cuts," said one gasoline trader in Houston.
"It could very well be voluntary," he added.
Coastal's Mitchell meanwhile said the unit was not hit by a fire, but exhibited problems while in operation that needed to be addressed. He did not elaborate.
But shipping sources said Coastal has been spotted since last Friday in tanker markets.
Sellers of prompt regular conventional gasoline in Houston were asking 0.50 cent more Tuesday morning at 3.50 cents under October NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures, or about 58.00 cents a gallon.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
